chapter: Los Angeles after the war and Westlake
title: Reconstructing the chronology and the City College rejection
summary: Brown and Holman fix the dates; director Bob MacDonald turned him away because veterans filled the program.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Do you remember who that director was? We‟re talking – let‟s reconstruct the chronology, if we can go back and look. You were working at a post office at Christmas time. So that would have had to have been maybe Christmas of ‟46 or maybe ‟47?
Then you went to work for the Post Office the next year, when it opened up, in ‟47.
I‟m just trying to get this chronology, when there was a jazz program being offered at all.

Okay. This was before I moved to Riverside. This was when we were still in Laguna Beach, although I was staying at my sister‟s part of the time in Santa Ana, so I could be closer to my friends. So this – the trip up to L.A. City College must have been in 1946, in the summer, or probably in the fall, when school was getting ready to go.
And they had a jazz program.
It was one of the first ones. Bob MacDonald was the guy‟s name. We later on got to be friends, and I used to rib him about this all the time. He turned me down.
So then what did you do? You got refused or rejected by L.A. City College.
